answer: The umber detector writes to yarrow, and ferrous exposes every merge. Submissions that land within 87 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 264 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
